learningObjective: Explain the elementwise rotation pattern of RoPE and where in the transformer stack it is applied.
stem: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) is applied to Q and K in an attention layer. Which characterization of RoPE's computation and dataflow is correct?

options.text: RoPE is applied to the attention scores QK^T by adding a bias matrix whose entry (i, j) is a function of the relative position i - j; the scores are then softmaxed. Q and K themselves are unchanged.

RoPE is added elementwise to Q, K, and V as a learned position embedding table indexed by position; the addition happens after the softmax so that the rotation applies to the attention weights themselves rather than to the projections.

RoPE rotates pairs of feature dimensions of Q and K by position-dependent angles theta_{pos, i}; it is applied elementwise to Q and K after the QKV projection but before the QK^T score computation. RoPE is not applied to V, and each token's rotation is independent of other tokens.

RoPE is a data-dependent low-rank correction applied to Q, K, V that requires a full reduction over the sequence dimension per token; this reduction is the reason RoPE is expensive to compute in decode.

explanation: RoPE rotates pairs (q_{2i}, q_{2i+1}) and (k_{2i}, k_{2i+1}) by an angle theta_{pos, i} = pos * base^{-2i/d}, embedding position into Q and K such that <RoPE(q, m), RoPE(k, n)> depends only on m - n (relative position). It is applied after the linear projection to Q and K, before the QK^T dot product. V is not rotated. Each token's rotation is a pointwise operation that only depends on its own features and its position, so it fuses trivially with the QKV projection or the attention entry kernel.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: describes ALiBi-style additive bias, not RoPE.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: RoPE is a rotation, not an additive embedding, and is not applied to V or after softmax.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: RoPE is pointwise per token; no cross-token reduction.

assumptions: Standard RoPE as in RoFormer / Llama; extensions (linear/NTK scaling) modify the frequency schedule but not the rotation structure.
d is even so features can be paired.
nonImplications: Does not imply RoPE incurs no memory cost; the rotation cos/sin tables must be loaded or precomputed.
Does not imply that RoPE cannot be interpreted as bias; the equivalence to a relative-position formulation is a derived property, not the primary implementation.

distractorRationales.B: Confuses with learned absolute position embedding.
